reading.body:
A single OpenStreetMap point tagged as a data center in Italy is most likely a mistagged professional-services office, not a real facility. The name Studio Delta Srl combines "Studio," an Italian term for a professional practice, with "Srl," the standard suffix for a limited-liability company. That naming pattern fits an architecture, engineering, accounting, or design firm, not a hosting or colocation business.

The record carries zero megawatts, no operator, no website, and no state or city. Those absences matter more than the tag itself. A genuine data center entry in this dataset would normally carry a power figure or an operator, and this one carries neither. The telecom=data_center tag most plausibly describes the firm's own office IT rather than a commercial facility.

For AI scaling, the point is a caution about the underlying map. Facility counts drawn from volunteered geographic data can include office closets and mislabeled businesses, so a raw count of tagged points is not a count of buildings that can host compute. This entry cannot be confirmed either way, because the research session hit search quota limits and the firm's actual line of business was never verified. It is filed as a probable mistag based on naming convention alone.

What the data does not show is how many other entries share this problem. One probable mistag says nothing about the error rate across the dataset, and it says nothing about Italy's real data center capacity. The nearest airport, Parma, at 19.5 miles, is the only geographic anchor given, and it does not establish that any facility exists at these coordinates.
